selector.rationale: Soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction on CT, along with avid enhancement on MRI, support Giant Cell Tumor diagnosis

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a well-defined, dense, and compact bone lesion, not matching the lytic lesion with soap-bubble appearance

rejected.label: Eosinophilic Granuloma
rejected.why: Usually presents with a single, well-defined lytic lesion, but the described lesion has a more complex appearance

rejected.label: Ewing's Sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more aggressive and permeative bone destruction pattern, and often with significant soft-tissue component and systemic symptoms

rejected.label: Brown Tumor
rejected.why: Although it has some similar imaging features, the clinical context and specific findings, such as the soap-bubble appearance, are more typical of Giant Cell Tumor
